claim: The receipt task uses real images with varied dimensions, blur, shadows, regional taxes, discounts, and rounding conventions.
The evaluator uses six deterministic checks over extracted receipt data rather than an LLM judge.
A failed positive-value check exposed a case where the model treated a discount as a purchased line item even though the final arithmetic still balanced.
Extraction, deterministic evaluation, and dashboard rendering are separate stages joined by saved JSON records.
Saving results after pipeline steps supports human inspection, resuming, incremental testing, and later golden datasets.
The team improved the prompt and output model on a small receipt set, then expanded the set to expose discounts, extraction failures, and other corner cases.
The speakers warn that prompt optimization can overfit when the eval definition is wrong or the real-world data has not been understood.
They propose using the same checks in production to retry specific failures and send unresolved cases to a human after a bounded number of attempts.
note: Proposed product design, not implemented by the checked-in evaluator.

claim: The final stored run processed 350 receipts, had 349 successful extractions, and had 327 receipts pass every check.
